windowTitle: Serial integration stage 6 - Workspace resolves the default OPL App order source from Runtime Control
scope: Prove the Workspace launch path resolves the default OPL App order source from the approved Runtime Release, stamping runtime_release provenance and fabricating no Build/Package/CapabilityVersion, and refusing an unapproved release. No production source, contract, schema or migration changed.
implemented: services/workspace/internal/launch/application_source_test.go: TestResolveApplicationSourceDefaultAppBuildsRuntimeReleaseDescriptor drives resolveApplicationSource over a paged RuntimeControlProductService stub with an approved Runtime Release whose publisher contract carries the immutable OCI and application revision template; it asserts the resolved selection is opl_app, the descriptor provenance is RUNTIME_RELEASE (never BUILD), the artifact and application revision are the release's own, the descriptor digest/object-ref are present, and an unapproved release is FailedPrecondition rather than substituted.

verification.environment: local loopback PostgreSQL container for the owner-migration tests
cases: TestResolveApplicationSourceDefaultAppBuildsRuntimeReleaseDescriptor: approved release -> opl_app source, RUNTIME_RELEASE provenance, release artifact/revision, descriptor identity; revoked release -> FailedPrecondition.
All existing Workspace launch and migration suites still pass.

notRun: No real Runtime Control, TKE cluster, Candidate build, Instance deployment or production readback.
The default App's real route activation (I07), the publisher opl-model-config/v1 applied readback (I08 serving half) and the full Console/BFF default-App business chain (I11) remain open.
claimBoundary: This receipt claims a Cloud source-level proof with a focused unit test: the Workspace launch path resolves the default OPL App source from an approved Runtime Release with runtime_release provenance and no Build lineage. It does not claim a Candidate, deployment or production acceptance.
